hooks.note: Swift let volumeView = MPVolumeView(frame: .zero). Its UISlider sets the Android media volume, and creating it makes the platform post SystemVolumeDidChange for media volume changes.
Swift var latestSetVolumeTime = ContinuousClock.now, a monotonic instant, not the wall clock.

Swift addObserver(Notification.Name("SystemVolumeDidChange"), #selector(handleSystemVolumeDidChange)). The generated Model.addObserver(name, selector) does nothing, so the selfie stick never saw a volume button press.

hooks.new: val volumeSlider = volumeView.subviews.firstOrNull { it is com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UISlider } as? com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UISlider ?: return; mainScope.launch { delay(100); latestSetVolumeTime = com.moblin.android.platform.core.ContinuousClock.now; volumeSlider.value = volume }
hooks.note: Swift setSystemVolume on one line: 0.1 seconds later on the main thread, remember the time and set the MPVolumeView slider, which sets the media volume.
Swift latestSetVolumeTime.duration(to: .now) > .seconds(1). The generated whole-second comparison needed two seconds before a press at minimum or maximum volume counted again.
